newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: OVER 4,000 WORKERS STRIKE AT S.AFRICAN TEA ESTATE.
newsitem.headline: OVER 4,000 WORKERS STRIKE AT S.AFRICAN TEA ESTATE.

text.p: The strike by more than 4,000 workers at South Africa's Sapekoe Tea Estate Ltd has entered its second week, halting production at several plantations.

South African Agricultural Plantation Allied Workers Union (Saapawu) members embarked on industrial action last Monday following a wage dispute with Sapekoe, one of South Africa's largest tea estates.
"The union is demanding an increase of 121 rand per month for lowest-paid workers who currently earn 193 rand per month," said Motlhabane Mogotsi, Saapawu's national organiser.
He said the company was offering a 10 percent increase. There was also a deadlock over the size of a 13th cheque.
Johan Grobler, Sapekoe's human resources manager, told Reuters that work at several tea estates in the Northern Province and KwaZulu-Natal where the union was represented had come to a standstill.
He declined to comment on the financial effects of the strike, but said work at the group's coffee plantations was proceeding normally.
Mogotsi said the statutory Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration (CCMA) had offered to assist the parties in solving the dispute. A meeting was scheduled for Friday.
However if CCMA action failed, the 45,000-strong union would request sister unions in the Congress of South African Trade Unions federation to pressure the company to settle the dispute.
"The kind of pressure will be determined by individual trade unions," Mogotsi said.
South African tea production is around 12,000 tonnes a year.
